title: MemoryBackend.update_object reports Ok(None) for every successful patch — never the (Some(obj)) server-set-fields path
description:
Trigger: client calls /set update modifying any property of an existing Metadata object. The MemoryBackend (memory.rs:856) returns Ok(None) for every successful update. The MetadataBackend trait doc on update_object (backend.rs:85-88) defines Some(obj)/None as a signal of whether the backend modified server-set properties beyond what the client requested (RFC 8620 §5.3 server-set field echo).

Because the MemoryBackend never returns Some(obj), the handle_metadata_set handler at metadata.rs:436-439 always writes Value::Null into the updated[id_str] slot. This is correct for the 'no server-set fields changed' case, which is in fact what's true for the MemoryBackend (it has no server-set fields beyond id).

But the integration tests have no coverage of the Some(obj) path. The handler's branch at metadata.rs:428-435 (Ok(Some(obj)) → serialize obj into updated map) is dead code under the current test suite. A future MetadataBackend impl that DOES modify server-set fields on update has no test demonstrating the wire shape it should produce.

Less acute than the filter no-op. Filing as P2 efficiency/test-coverage gap, not P0 correctness.
close_reason: Triage 2026-10-31 at c07d5206: moot: metadata-server MemoryBackend/update_object and Metadata/set handler deleted in b34a07bf (draft-02 rewrite); crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/ is now only changes.rs/filter.rs/validate.rs/lib.rs (lib.rs:1-8)
